title: NASA Publications
slide_intent: Teach editors to identify the origin of a publication and choose pictures according to what the reader must learn from them.
strategic_value: NASA can give very different publications a common origin while allowing technical diagrams and cover illustrations to serve different purposes.
demonstration: Three columns introduce the publications program, identification, use of the logotype inside a recurring title, image selection and typography. This opening page teaches through text.
practical_value: Decide where to credit NASA and whether a publication calls for an evocative cover image or a precise technical illustration.

content_islands.name: Program and identification
content_islands.spec: Begin the three-column text with the section heading. Follow the program rationale with the logotype requirements, carrying the text into the next column.

content_islands.name: Recurring titles
content_islands.spec: Give the stem-word convention its own subheading. Explain the limits on using NASA as part of a recurring publication title.

content_islands.name: Image and type guidance
content_islands.spec: Use short subheads for illustration and photography, then typography. Keep the running column order when the image guidance continues into the last column.
